To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated that a highly scalable appearance-only SLAMS system can be built, that it can be applied to very large scale environments (1000 km), and that the system is robust to aliasing and perceptual aliasing (i.e. the system is robust against the same appearance being seen at multiple locations).

1) FAB-MAP can be extended to operate in a very large scale setting, 2) the system can be implemented using a sparse approximation to FAB-MAP suitable for use in an inverted index, 3) a 1, 000 km trajectory is more than an oder of magnitude longer than any previously reported appearance-only SLAM result, and 4) the system is fully probabilistic, incorporating a robustness to perceptual aliasing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of building a large-scale map of the appearance of the world.
building a large-scale appearance-based navigation system.
the development of a highly scalable and robust system for appearance mapping and loop detection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have shown that appearance based SLAM can work on a very large scale and is suitable for practical use.
this work represents the state of the art in appearance-based SLAM.
this paper describes the first appearance-only SLAM system capable of navigating in large-scale environments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first appearance-based SLAM system that is capable of operating on very large data sets.
we have developed an appearance-only SLAM algorithm that can handle very large scale data sets.
we have demonstrated the first appearance-only system that is suitable for very large-scale navigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the problem of large scale appearance-based localization is well defined, solvable, and has a clear solution.

appearance-based localization can scale to very large data sets, and that it is now possible to build systems that can navigate over very large distances using only appearance information, without reference to the metric structure of the scene.
appearance-only SLAM is not only possible, but also practical for large-scale outdoor navigation.
